model.title: Schematic VSEPR geometry: methane, ammonia and water
model.description: Unqualified proposal for human review. Static coordinate construction with species-dependent geometry; viewer angle measurements use the same atom centres.
assumptions: Species input is discrete: 0=CH4, 1=NH3, 2=H2O; illustrative default 0. Lone-pair and angle-annotation inputs are binary, default 1.
Fixed representative H–central–H angles: methane arccos(-1/3), approximately 109.5 degrees; ammonia 107 degrees; water 104.5 degrees. These are teaching values, not predictions.
Central atom is at (origin,origin,origin). H1=(radial,origin,height); H2=(side_x,side_y,height); H3=(side_x,negative_side_y,height); H4=(origin,origin,top).
H1 and H2 are always present. H3 and its bond use nonwater visibility; H4 and its bond use methane visibility. Central identity follows the same species selector.
A schematic lone-pair region along the H4 direction uses lone_top visibility. A second along the H3 direction uses lone_side visibility; absent hydrogen bonds are hidden.
Illustrative normalized bond length is represented by 1 m of scene distance, not a physical molecular length. Fixed schematic sphere sizes may use this scene scale.

Four electron regions are represented by four direction slots. Tetrahedral electron-region geometry is a classification, not a claim that all ammonia or water region angles equal the ideal tetrahedral angle.
Angle annotations use the viewer's three-centre angle measurement on visible hydrogen–central–hydrogen centres. pair_cosine independently checks the representative H1–central–H2 geometry.
Angular constants are dimensionless radians; display_scale=57.29577951308232 and display_unit=degrees. Visibility and camera changes do not change coordinates.
Steady geometry only: time_experiment=null. Selection, rotation, zoom and explanatory comparisons are viewer interactions, not physical predictions.
limitations: Schematic VSEPR geometry, not calculated quantum orbitals, electron-density surfaces or directly measured lone-pair boundaries.
Lone-pair angular influence and angle compression are explained qualitatively; no quantitative repulsion law derives the supplied angles.
No quantum calculations, energetics, vibrations, environmental effects, accurate radii or physical bond lengths. Scope is representative static isolated molecules.
The scalar operator set has no inverse cosine. Degree measurements must use the available spatial-centre angle tool, not disconnected scalar angle labels.
Only the three discrete species and binary visibility settings are supported. Atom and bond selection and guided comparisons require downstream explanatory content.

snapshot.unfinished_question: Why are methane, ammonia and water different shapes? Build an interactive CBSE Class 11 VSEPR molecular-geometry experience with manipulable 3D methane, ammonia and water models. Let me rotate and zoom the molecules, switch species, select atoms and bonds, and show or hide schematic lone-pair regions. Show actual bond arrangements and bond-angle measurements consistent with their standard approximate geometries. Explain the difference between electron-region geometry and molecular shape, with guided comparisons. Clearly label the model as schematic VSEPR geometry, not calculated quantum orbitals. Use schematic spheres and bonds with parameter-driven coordinates and visibility; the existing viewer supplies selection, rotation and zoom.

definition.title: Schematic VSEPR geometry: methane, ammonia and water
definition.description: Compare atom arrangements and four electron regions. Rotate, zoom and select with the viewer; lone-pair regions are schematic, not calculated quantum orbitals.

parts.label: Species
parts.explanation: Schematic readout overview. Discrete allowed values 0=CH4, 1=NH3, 2=H2O; default 0.

parts.label: Show lone pairs
parts.explanation: Schematic readout overview. Binary 0 or 1; default 1. Changes schematic region visibility only.

parts.label: Show angle measurements
parts.explanation: Schematic readout overview. Binary 0 or 1; default 1. Changes spatial measurement annotation visibility only.

parts.label: Coordinate-derived angle cosine
parts.explanation: Schematic readout overview. H1–central–H2 cosine from the same coordinates; between -0.334 and -0.250. Viewer supplies degree measurement.

limits: Only CH4, NH3 and H2O; species values 0, 1 and 2 and binary visibility controls are supported.
Representative static isolated molecules only; no quantum calculations, energetics, vibrations or environmental effects.
Scene bond length 1 and sphere sizes are illustrative, not physical bond lengths or accurate atomic radii.
Coordinate-based viewer angle measurements must use visible hydrogen centres and the central centre: approximately 109.5°, 107° and 104.5°. The scalar model has no inverse cosine.
Lone-pair regions are schematic, not orbitals, electron-density surfaces or measured boundaries.
Four electron regions have tetrahedral VSEPR classification; not every direction pair in ammonia or water has the ideal tetrahedral angle.
Lone-pair angular compression is qualitative; no repulsion law predicts the supplied angles.

Eleven geometry parts total; at most nine visible: methane nine, ammonia eight and water seven with lone pairs shown. Measurement annotations are viewer overlays, not extra molecular parts aimed at representing matter except atoms, bonds and lone pairs do already do so schematically. Hide absent hydrogens and their bonds together, and exclude hidden parts from selection and measurement before use.

parts.label: Central atom: C / N / O
parts.explanation: Carbon, nitrogen or oxygen sits at the centre of the selected molecule. Each has four electron regions: spaces occupied by bonds or lone pairs.

parts.label: Hydrogen 1
parts.explanation: This hydrogen is present in all three molecules. Its centre helps define the measured bond angle.

parts.label: Hydrogen 2
parts.explanation: This hydrogen is present in all three molecules. The angle between its bond and hydrogen 1's bond is measured at the central atom.

parts.label: Hydrogen 3
parts.explanation: This hydrogen appears in methane and ammonia. Water has a lone-pair region in this direction instead.

parts.label: Hydrogen 4
parts.explanation: This hydrogen appears only in methane. Ammonia and water have a lone-pair region in this direction instead.

parts.label: Bond to hydrogen 1
parts.explanation: This bond represents electrons shared with hydrogen 1. A bond counts as one electron region.

parts.label: Bond to hydrogen 2
parts.explanation: This bond represents electrons shared with hydrogen 2. Together with bond 1 it marks the measured angle.

parts.label: Bond to hydrogen 3
parts.explanation: This bond appears in methane and ammonia. It is absent in water.

parts.label: Bond to hydrogen 4
parts.explanation: This bond appears only in methane. Methane has four bonding regions and no lone pairs on carbon.

parts.label: Top lone-pair region
parts.explanation: Ammonia and water have a lone pair here: two electrons not shared in a bond. This region is a schematic reminder, not a calculated orbital.

parts.label: Second lone-pair region
parts.explanation: Water has a second lone pair in this direction. Lone pairs count toward electron-region geometry, but molecular shape describes atom positions.

experiments.title: Four bonds
experiments.prompt: Predict methane's shape, then select methane, rotate and zoom, and inspect its bonds.
experiments.explanation: Methane has four bonding regions and tetrahedral molecular shape. In View tools, choose Measure an angle, then Hydrogen 1, Central atom, Hydrogen 2. The representative angle is approximately 109.5 degrees; pair_cosine uses the same coordinates. This is schematic VSEPR geometry, not molecular sizes or quantum orbitals.

experiments.title: One lone pair
experiments.prompt: Predict whether ammonia has the same shape and angle as methane, then switch species and measure. Show lone-pair regions and inspect them.
experiments.explanation: Ammonia has three bonding regions and one lone pair: tetrahedral electron-region classification but trigonal-pyramidal molecular shape. Its supplied representative angle is 107 degrees. Lone-pair angular influence is qualitative, not a calculated repulsion law.

experiments.title: Two lone pairs
experiments.prompt: Predict water's shape and bond-angle ordering, then switch to water and measure. Predict whether hiding lone-pair regions will change that angle, then check.
experiments.explanation: Water has two bonding regions and two lone pairs, bent molecular shape and a supplied angle of 104.5 degrees. Hiding regions changes visibility only, not coordinates or pair_cosine. Regions are not measured boundaries or electron-density surfaces. Molecular shape describes atom positions; not all region directions have ideal tetrahedral angles.

controls.help: Switch species to change atom arrangement, bond presence and the coordinate-derived angle cosine.
Hide or show schematic lone-pair regions without changing atom positions or bond angles.
This unused input does not control annotations. Use View tools, Measure an angle, then Hydrogen 1, Central atom, Hydrogen 2.

coverage.explanation: Species selects coordinates for tetrahedral methane, trigonal-pyramidal ammonia and bent water; pair_cosine checks their geometry. Viewer rotation and zoom support inspection.

Species changes coordinates and matching atom and bond presence. Independent show_lone changes only region visibility; it has no causal path to pair_cosine. Viewer selection supports atom and bond inspection.

Species-dependent coordinates yield representative angles of approximately 109.5, 107 and 104.5 degrees. Measure manually using View tools, Measure an angle, then Hydrogen 1, Central atom, Hydrogen 2; pair_cosine is the coordinate-derived check.
Four electron regions give tetrahedral electron-region classification in all three species. Molecular shape describes atom positions, excluding lone-pair regions.

Compare four bonds, three bonds plus one lone pair, and two bonds plus two lone pairs. Stronger lone-pair angular influence explains compression qualitatively; the static model supplies angles rather than predicting them from repulsion.

outcomes: Inspect and compare tetrahedral methane, trigonal-pyramidal ammonia and bent water using rotatable, zoomable 3D models.
Switch species, select atoms and bonds, and toggle schematic lone-pair regions without changing the underlying bond geometry.
Measure representative H–central-atom–H angles of approximately 109.5° for methane, 107° for ammonia and 104.5° for water.
Distinguish the tetrahedral electron-region arrangement shared by all three species from molecular shape, which describes atom positions.

Explain qualitatively how four bonding regions, three bonding regions plus one lone pair, and two bonding regions plus two lone pairs produce different shapes; compare the stronger angular influence of lone-pair regions.

generation_quality.scope: Recipe, label, connection and dependency checks only. Dependency paths do not prove numeric change. Overlap, recognizability, physical correctness and child usability require separate evaluation.

visual.scope: Eight fitted views; projected bounds, center-ray occlusion, conservative bounding-box overlaps and estimated two-line label capacity. These heuristics do not replace rendered-image or child usability review.

sampled_quality.scope: Defaults, five points per input plus presets, a midpoint context for apparently inactive controls, all-input endpoints, and lesson experiments. Finite geometry and observed changes only; no proof of scientific accuracy, recognizability or complete state-space coverage.

repair_actions.rule: Retries require the existing explicit retry flow. Never edit accepted artifact hashes or automatically spend provider requests.

scene_revision.feedback: Keep the accepted model, assembly, geometry and correct bond angles unchanged. Correct learning controls: species must use kind choices with only Methane (CH4)=0, Ammonia (NH3)=1, Water (H2O)=2; show_lone must use kind choices with Hide=0 and Show=1. No sliders or fractional values for these choices. The existing show_angles input does not drive a visual annotation: include its control with visible=false and do not claim it automatically displays angles. Explain the real supported measurement: View tools, Measure an angle, then Hydrogen 1, Central atom, Hydrogen 2. Keep guided species comparisons and lone-pair explanations, and explicitly say schematic VSEPR geometry, not molecular sizes or quantum orbitals.
